:JUDGMENT:
The present petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 13.01.2021 when the emanates have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Munivenkatappa in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2248/2021

During the stage of trial, the original Petitioner died and his LRs were brought on record as Petitioner No.1(a) and Petitioner No.1(b) and the amendment was carried out and amended petition was filed.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1a is the wife and petitioner No.1b is the daughter of deceased Munivenkatappa who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 07.10.2021 due to the negligence of the driver of the respondent's Eicher canter.

It is submitted that on 13.01.2021 at about 1.35 p.m., deceased Munivenkatappa was waiting to cross the road on left side of the road on NH-75,
Hoskote - Kolar road, near Devika Suzuki show room, Hoskote town, Bengaluru rural district, at that time, the respondents Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-6519 which was driven by its driver rashly and negligently with high speed, endangering human life and dashed against the deceased.
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2248/2021

As a result of the collision, the deceased sustained severe head injuries and other injuries and subsequently was taken to Srinivasa Specialty hospital, Hoskote,
Siddartha Hospital, Nelamangala, Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.
Pertinently, the injuries suffered by the Munivenkatappa were fatal and unable to recover he died on 07.10.2021.
Consequent to the accident, on 13.01.2021 FIR No.16/2021
was registered with the Hoskote Police station under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the Respondent No.1.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Eicher lorry.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 40 Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
2 years and working as a Coolie and an agriculturist was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2248/2021 petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.15,50,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 has remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that the deceased himself was tort feasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the policy of insurance issued by this respondent subject to the terms and conditions, expectations and limitations.

The age, occupation and the income of the deceased and manner of the accident and vehicle involved in the accident and the cause of death are denied and the petitioners are called upon to prove the same.
It is submitted that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2248/2021 without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. Vide order dated 17.07.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Munivenkatappa S/o Late Kariyappa was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.01.2021 at about 1.35 p.m., on NH-75, Bengaluru - Kolar Service road, near Devika Suzuki Showroom, Hoskote Town, Bengaluru District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Eicher Canter Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-6519 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Munivenkatappa?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If yes,
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2248/2021 what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4) What Order or Award?

5. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants have examined petitioner No.1a as PW1 and other two witnesses examined as PW-2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.24 documents and the respondent No.2 has got examined its Proposal Manager as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1 and 2.
Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
3 6.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2248/2021  REASONS 7.
Issue No.1:
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioners that, petitioner No.1(a) is examined as PW.1.

She has deposed about the manner of the accident and stated that on 13.01.2021 at about 1.35 p.m. when the deceased was waiting to cross the road on the left side of the road on NH-75 road, Hoskote - Kolar road, the Eicher Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53- D-6519( hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) dashed the deceased resulting in the accident.
The deceased has sustained severe injuries and was under going followup treatment.
It is submitted that even after discharge from the hospital he was taking followup treatment and his legs were infected due to the injuries and he was bedridden.
There was heavy infection in his legs and hence he died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

As far as manner of the accident is concerned the petitioner in addition to her oral evidence has produced Ex.P1 which is the FIR which discloses that the case has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle and SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2248/2021 Ex.P3 is the wound certificate and the after investigation the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of offending vehicle punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

The charge sheet document disclose that the deceased was the pillion rider and the accident took place when he was crossing the road along with box filled with spare parts and the driver of the offending vehicle hit the deceased resulting in the accident.

8. As far as manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent and PW.1 has denied that the accident took place due to the fault of her husband and denied that the accident took place since her husband crossed the road without seeing the oncoming vehicles.

Except the said suggestion nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to dispute the manner of the accident and to prove that the accident has taken place due to the fault of the deceased.

Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence it is satisfactorily established that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2248/2021 offending vehicle.

The petitioners have also got examined the MRO of Victoria hospital as PW.2 who has produced the case sheet to show the treatment given to the deceased Munivenkatappa for the injuries sustained in the RTA and also examined PW.3 MRO of Siddartha hospital to show the treatment obtained for the injuries sustained in the RTA.
The respondents though not seriously disputed the accident however have seriously disputed that the death of the Munivenkatappa was caused due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

In this regard RW.1 on behalf of respondent No.2 has submitted that there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and the subsequent death and stated that there is no PM report and the police have not invoked Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
4 Sec.304A of IPC against the driver of the offending vehicle and hence the death of Munivenkatappa is due to other ailments and not due to accidental injuries.

9. In this regard RW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for petitioner and RW.1 has admitted that SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2248/2021 Munivenkatappa had sustained grievous injuries and he had gangrene to both his legs which was caused due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

As far as failure to conduct postmortem is concerned it is submitted that Munivenkatappa died in the year 2021 during the Covid pandamic and hence it was not possible to conduct PM report of the deceased.

In this regard on perusal of wound certificate that is on 28.08.2021 of Srinivasa hospital it discloses that above patient was brought to the hospital with the history of RTA and on his examination he had degloving injury extending to the right ankle foot and muscle was exposed and tendon exposed and punctured wound over 1/3rd of left leg and he had sustained fracture to right humerus and commuted fracture of left leg bone and fracture of multiple phalanges of right toe which are obviously grievous injuries.

The medical records discloses that he has spent amount towards treatment and the medical records discloses that he has undergone treatment in two hospitals and was taking treatment was almost up to month of March.
As per the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2248/2021 medical bills he has been taking medicines and undertaking medical treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.

Hence, in the absence of clear evidence to show that the deceased died due to some other ailments there is clinching evidence to show Munivenkatappa died due to the accidental injuries and he died unable to recover from the accidental injuries.
As far as the PM report is concerned it can be accepted that since the deceased died during the Covid pandemic it was not possible to conduct PM report of the deceased.

In addition the status of the deceased also discloses that he was labourer and was obtaining treatment at government hospital and probably was not in a possible to spend considerable amount towards his treatment and injuries sustained where of such a nature which could not be cured completely and only be treated temporarily.
Hence, there is evidence to show that the deceased Munivenkatappa died due to accidental injuries and hence petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of Munivenkatappa in the RTA.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2248/2021 in the "Affirmative ".
10. Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1a and 1b are the wife and daughter of the deceased Munivenkatappa.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P14 to 16 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1a & b and deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
11. The Petitioner No.1a and b are the wife and daughter of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Munivenkatappa have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Munivenkatappa and also they have proved that the death of the Munivenkatappa has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2248/2021 12. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:

sentences.text: 1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 40 years.
Ex.P-11 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 05.07.1979.
The alleged accident has taken place on 13.01.2021.
Hence, by considering Ex.P14, the age of the deceased is taken as 40 years.
13. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a Coolie and an agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence or adduced the evidence of the employer or any salary payment receipts to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2248/2021 prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,000X 12= 1,80,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,80,000/-.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
6
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2248/2021 Moving forward with the issue of future prospects

,
the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.
14. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife and daughter.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2248/2021 members is 2 to 3. 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
15. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 40 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,000/- comes to Rs.6,000/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,000/- p.m. (Rs.15,000/- + Rs.6,000/- =
Rs.21,000/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 15.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that, if the deceased was bachelor, half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

16. After deducting 1/3rd of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,000/- it comes to Rs.14,000/- (21,000/- - 7,000/-) and multiplier applied is 15, (Rs.14,000/- x SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2248/2021 12 = 1,68,000/-, Rs.1,68,000/- x 15 = 25,20,000/-).

Thus, the Petitioners are Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
7 entitled for compensation of Rs.25,20,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Medical expenses:
The petitioners have produced Ex.P12 in all 64 medical bills and petitioners are entitled amount of Rs.1,25,907/-
under this head.
17. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads,
namely, 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.
15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2248/2021 applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.

Further,
the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

In view of the foregoing reasons and discussions, the petitioners are entitled compensation amount of Rs.27,79,007/-.

18. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-6519.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2248/2021 Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

19. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

20. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1a and b are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,79,007/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed SCCH 15 23 MVC No.2248/2021 to pass the following :

4. Vide order dated 17.07.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Munivenkatappa S/o Late Kariyappa was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.01.2021 at about 1.35 p.m., on NH-75, Bengaluru - Kolar Service road, near Devika Suzuki Showroom, Hoskote Town, Bengaluru District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Eicher Canter Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-6519 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Munivenkatappa?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes,
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2248/2021 what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4) What Order or Award?
18. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-6519.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence it is satisfactorily established that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2248/2021 offending vehicle.
As far as failure to conduct postmortem is concerned it is submitted that Munivenkatappa died in the year 2021 during the Covid pandamic and hence it was not possible to conduct PM report of the deceased.
As per the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2248/2021 medical bills he has been taking medicines and undertaking medical treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence, in the absence of clear evidence to show that the deceased died due to some other ailments there is clinching evidence to show Munivenkatappa died due to the accidental injuries and he died unable to recover from the accidental injuries.
As far as the PM report is concerned it can be accepted that since the deceased died during the Covid pandemic it was not possible to conduct PM report of the deceased.
In addition the status of the deceased also discloses that he was labourer and was obtaining treatment at government hospital and probably was not in a possible to spend considerable amount towards his treatment and injuries sustained where of such a nature which could not be cured completely and only be treated temporarily.
Hence, there is evidence to show that the deceased Munivenkatappa died due to accidental injuries and hence petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of Munivenkatappa in the RTA.
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 40 years.
The alleged accident has taken place on 13.01.2021.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence or adduced the evidence of the employer or any salary payment receipts to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2248/2021 prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,000X 12= 1,80,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,80,000/-.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
6
,
the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

17. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.
By SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2248/2021 applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further,
the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.
In light of the above discussion, the claimants are awarded compensation as follows:
. Head amount 1 Income per annum Rs.1,80,000/-
 Rs.15,000X12 2 Future prospects 40% ie Rs.21,000/-
 Rs.15,000+ Rs.6,000/-
 =Rs.21,000/- pm.
3
Loss of dependency (A) Rs.25,20,000/-
6  Funeral expenses (B) Rs. 18,150/-
7  Loss of estate (C) Rs. 18,150/-
8 Medical expenses incurred for Rs. 1,25,907/-
 the treatment of deceased (D)
9  Loss of consortium (E)
 (a)spousal and filial  consortium Rs. 96,800/-
Total Compensation awarded Rs.27,79,007/- (A+B+C+D+E)
In view of the foregoing reasons and discussions, the petitioners are entitled compensation amount of Rs.27,79,007/-.
SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2248/2021 Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1a and b are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,79,007/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed SCCH 15 23 MVC No.2248/2021 to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1(a) and 1(b) are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,79,007/-
along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition Munivenkatappa vs Akram Sha on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34221252/
9 till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1(a) and 1(b) are SCCH 15 24 MVC No.2248/2021 apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 90% to the Petitioner No.1a 2) 10% to the Petitioner No.1b After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1a, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1a by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1a in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1b is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.1b shall be released to her by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
